description: Agent Onboarding: submit the wallet a new agent is set up with, before it needs one: optionally the agent with its id and when it runs its first task; the job with whether it moves money, the most it needs the wallet to hold (such as the first month’s spend), its unit, the network it pays on and the asset it pays in; the wallet with its id or address, its kind (a wallet for this agent alone, one shared with other agents, the owner’s own wallet, the treasury or not known), network, asset, balance, unit, when it was set up and when funds first moved into it; the recovery with who recorded it (the owner, an operator, the agent itself, nobody or not known), when, how the wallet is recovered and the recovery note as written, read for a seed phrase or key written out in it; and optionally the share above the job’s need at which a balance counts as overfunded (20 when left out). The signed report gives the wallet with its balance as a share of what the job needs, the recovery with whether it was written out and whether it came before funding, every requirement (a wallet for this agent alone, funded to what the job needs, on the job’s network and asset, recovery recorded by the owner, recovery recorded before funds move, set up before the first task) as met, unmet or unknown, and counts them, and names an unsafe wallet: the agent drawing on a shared, owner or treasury wallet, no recovery, a recovery held by the agent, funds moved in before the recovery was recorded and a seed phrase or key written out in the note; then a balance past the headroom, another network or asset, a wallet set up or funded after the first task, an empty wallet and a recovery recorded by an operator, with the fix for each. When the job moves no money, no funds should be held. This reads one new agent’s wallet before funds move, beside the wallet tools already in the catalog: a month of an address’s activity is wever_wallet-statement and its recent flows wever_wallet-activity-brief, concentration caps across balances are wever_treasury-policy-check, an operator’s key recovery is wever_recovery-readiness-check and a budget’s five controls are wever_budget-controls-check. Verdict onboarding_wallet_unsafe, onboarding_wallet_partial, onboarding_wallet_unverified or onboarding_wallet_ready. POST /api/onboarding-wallet-check. Reads only the recorded onboarding material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; no credential is issued, rotated or revoked, no permission granted or removed, no wallet funded or moved, no limit set and the agent is not approved, and a credential found in supplied text is named by kind and never repeated. Agent Onboarding reads the setup of a new agent joining a system, before its first task: whether its identity is established and tied to its owner, whether its credentials are scoped to its job, stored where they belong and kept out of prompts, logs and shared documents, whether its wallet is the right one, funded only to the job with recovery recorded by the owner before funds move, whether its permissions match the written job, whether its limits sit in code with a human handoff, whether the systems it needs are provisioned and tested, whether it is ready for its first task and whether the onboarding record matches what is live. It is not vetting an outside party (wever_counterparty-onboarding-check reads a counterparty’s onboarding packet before the system transacts with it; an onboarding check reads an agent joining the system itself), not a grant or an authority for one action (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether a principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check whether an actor’s access fits its grant for an action; an onboarding check reads that the grant and the authority were put in place before the first task, and does not re-check them per action), not a limit in flight (the wever_limit checks and wever_agent-budget-guard read limits for work already running; an onboarding check reads that limits were set in code before it starts) and not an action’s consequences (the wever_risk checks read one planned action; an onboarding check reads readiness to start). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-onboarding-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-onboarding/.

starts_at.description: When the agent runs its first task.

headroom_percent.description: A balance more than this share above what the job needs counts as overfunded; 20 when left out.

asset.description: The asset the job pays in.

moves_money.description: The job moves money, so it needs a wallet.

needs.description: The most the job needs the wallet to hold, such as the first month’s spend.

network.description: The network the job pays on.

unit.description: The unit amounts are counted in, such as USDC.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

method.description: How the wallet is recovered, such as a recovery key the owner holds offline.

note.description: The recovery note as written, read for a seed phrase or key written out in it.

recorded_by.description: Who recorded how the wallet is recovered: the owner, an operator, the agent itself, nobody, or not known.

funded_at.description: When funds first moved into it.

kind.description: A wallet for this agent alone, one shared with other agents, the owner’s own wallet, the treasury, or not known.

unit.description: Its unit; the job’s when left out.

name: wever_onboarding-wallet-check
title: Onboarding wallet check
